research_problem: Security API misuse (crypto, SSL/TLS, OAuth) is widespread and dangerous, but research on detecting it is dispersed without synthesis
technical_approach: Kitchenham SLR over Scopus, IEEE Xplore and ACM DL (Nov 2022, no year limit) with CORE/Scimago venue filter plus snowballing; data extraction form and thematic synthesis
primary_contribution: First SLR of security API misuse detection: API and misuse taxonomies, detection-technique taxonomy, evaluation practices and 14 open issues
dataset_benchmark: 69 primary studies (2012-2022; 27 from search, rest via snowballing)
key_findings: 6 security API types (crypto 31, SSL/TLS 14, OAuth 9); 30 misuse types, mostly Android/Java; detection overwhelmingly heuristic (static 42, dynamic 9, hybrid 13) with only 3 ML studies; 9 public benchmarks, only 5 misuse-specific and all Java crypto/SSL, mostly synthetic and static; developers often reject misuses in non-sensitive contexts or without exploits; usability, repair, LLM use and API-evolution adaptation under-explored
author_limitations: Possible missed studies; subjective selection bias; extraction errors mitigated by DEF and meetings
analyst_limitations: Search ended Nov 2022 yet published 2025, missing LLM-era work; heavy reliance on snowballing; count inconsistencies (10 vs 11 metrics; 66 vs 64 heuristic); venue filter instead of quality appraisal; no agreement statistics; web/REST API security misuse largely out of scope
reproducibility: High: study list and extraction form in online appendix
suggested_extensions: Empirical study of LLM-generated security API misuse and LLM detectors; web API client-side security misuse taxonomy; context-aware triage with exploit demonstration; evolution-aware detection and versioned benchmarks; real multi-language dynamic benchmarks; LLM-based verified repair
evidence_location: Method p.4-6; RQ1 p.6-10; RQ2 p.12-18; RQ3 p.19-27; RQ4 p.27-29; open issues p.29-33; threats p.33
integrity: Tables 3, 5-7 column-split; figures missing; misuse list partially read
